short: A grouped set of business expenses an employee submits for approval and reimbursement.
seoTitle: Expense Report — Meaning, Contents and Process
metaDescription: An expense report groups the business costs an employee paid personally into one submission for approval and reimbursement. What it contains and how it flows.
definition: An expense report is a grouped submission of business costs an employee paid personally — travel, meals, fuel, supplies — presented with supporting bills for approval and reimbursement, and posted to the relevant expense accounts once approved.
bodyHtml:
What belongs on one

Each line carries a date, an amount, a category, a business purpose and a reference to the supporting bill. The purpose is the line most often left blank and the one an auditor asks about first, because a bill on its own shows that money was spent, not that it was spent for the business.

The approval chain

Submission, review against the expense policy, approval, reimbursement, and posting to the books. The control sits at the review step: a limit enforced before the money is reimbursed is worth more than a report produced after it. Where nobody spends company money except the owner, there is no claim to approve and a simple expense log does the same job at no cost.

Reimbursement is not an expense twice

The expense is recognised when the cost is incurred; the reimbursement settles a liability to the employee. Recording both as expenses double-counts the same rupee, which is the most common error when claims are handled outside the accounting system.

faq.question: How is an expense report different from an expense entry in the books?
faq.answer: An expense report is a claim submitted by a person and awaiting approval. The book entry is what happens after approval, when the cost is posted to an account and the amount owed to the employee is settled.

faq.question: Does a small business need expense reports?
faq.answer: Only if people other than the owner spend company money. With a single spender there is nothing to approve, and a categorised expense log answers the same question with less process.
